title: Third Meeting of India-Cambodia Joint Working Group on Trade and Investment (JWGTI) Held in Phnom Penh, Cambodia
subtitle: India-Cambodia Bilateral Trade Grows Over 36% to USD 406.78 Million in 2025-26
body_text:
The Third Meeting of the India-Cambodia Joint Working Group on Trade and Investment (JWGTI) was held on 24 August 2026 in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. The meeting was co-chaired by Shri Amit Verma, Joint Secretary, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, India, and Mr. Long Kemvichet, Director General of International Trade, Ministry of Commerce, Cambodia.
Both sides noted the encouraging momentum in bilateral trade, which grew by over 36% to reach USD 406.78 million in 2025-26, up from USD 299 million in the previous financial year, with the April-June 2026 quarter recording a further 63.25% year-on-year growth. Cambodia is currently India's 8th largest trading partner in ASEAN, accounting for 0.31% of India's total trade with the bloc, reflecting significant headroom for growth.
The meeting deliberated upon ways to diversify and deepen trade, including through cooperation and collaboration in traditional medicine, e-governance modules, recognition of Indian pharmacopeia, trade statistics reconciliation and the sharing of information on flagship trade fairs and business delegations.
The meeting also welcomed the successful launch of UPI acceptance at KHQR-enabled merchants in Phnom Penh on 2 June 2026, and discussed the next phase of enabling Cambodian payment applications to scan UPI QR codes in India, which would allow Cambodian travellers to use UPI-enabled terminals in India seamlessly.
The meeting further welcomed the agreement between both sides on the MoU on Custom Cooperation and discussed early signing, which would bring uniformity in custom procedure.
The two sides further discussed cooperation in agriculture and market access issues, expanding trade in dyes and pigments, banking and insurance sector cooperation. The two sides also welcomed the discussion for completion of the Bilateral Investment Treaty between India and Cambodia and agreed for early signature on it.
This was the third meeting of the JWGTI since its institutionalisation and the meeting reaffirmed the depth and growing potential of the India-Cambodia trade and economic partnership. The next meeting of the JWGTI will be held in India in 2027.
On the sidelines of the 3rd India–Cambodia JWGTI meeting, Shri Amit Verma had a productive call with H.E. Tith Rithipol, Under Secretary of State, Cambodia. Discussions covered strengthening bilateral trade and investment, cooperation in pharmaceuticals, and the successful UPI–KHQR digital payments linkage. Both sides reiterated their shared commitment for deepening the partnership between the countries.
Shri Amit Verma also met with members of the Indian Business Chamber in Cambodia (IBCC). Discussions focused on accelerating bilateral trade agreement discussions, facilitating Indian investment in Cambodia, and identifying 5–7 priority sectors including education, healthcare, IT, agriculture and tourism.
The meeting also discussed an “Invest in Cambodia” roadshow in India, positioning Cambodia as a production base for Indian companies seeking access to ASEAN markets, and establishing a mechanism for IBCC/FICCI/JBC to provide private-sector feedback to the JWGTI.
***
Abhishek Dayal/Garima Singh

enrichment.summary: India and Cambodia held the Third Joint Working Group on Trade and Investment (JWGTI) meeting in Phnom Penh on 24 August 2026, co-chaired by Joint Secretary Amit Verma and Cambodia's Director General Long Kemvichet. Bilateral trade grew over 36% to USD 406.78 million in 2025-26, with further 63.25% growth in Q1 2026-27. The two sides discussed a Customs Cooperation MoU, a Bilateral Investment Treaty, UPI-KHQR payment linkage expansion, and cooperation in pharmaceuticals, agriculture, and banking.
enrichment.context: Cambodia is a relatively small but fast-growing trade partner for India within ASEAN, currently ranked 8th among ASEAN partners and accounting for just 0.31% of India's total ASEAN trade, indicating significant untapped potential. This JWGTI mechanism, institutionalised to deepen trade ties, is part of India's broader 'Act East Policy' aimed at strengthening economic engagement with Southeast Asia beyond the India-ASEAN Free Trade Agreement framework. The push to extend UPI acceptance to Cambodia (via KHQR interoperability) follows a pattern of India expanding UPI's international footprint to countries like Singapore, UAE, Bhutan, Nepal, and Sri Lanka, positioning UPI as a tool of digital public infrastructure diplomacy. The proposed Bilateral Investment Treaty (BIT) is significant because India has been renegotiating investment treaties globally since adopting its 2016 Model BIT, which emphasizes host-state regulatory space and requires exhaustion of local remedies before international arbitration. Discussions on positioning Cambodia as a production base for Indian firms targeting ASEAN markets also reflect a 'China+1' supply chain diversification trend and India's interest in leveraging Cambodia's preferential access arrangements with other markets.

prelims_questions.question: The Joint Working Group on Trade and Investment (JWGTI) discussed in a recent India-Cambodia meeting is a mechanism primarily aimed at strengthening cooperation under which broader Indian foreign policy framework?
prelims_questions.explanation: India's engagement with ASEAN countries like Cambodia, including trade and investment cooperation, falls under India's Act East Policy, which succeeded the Look East Policy to deepen ties with Southeast and East Asia.

prelims_questions.question: UPI's international interoperability, as discussed in the India-Cambodia JWGTI meeting through linkage with KHQR, is an example of India's use of which of the following?
prelims_questions.explanation: India has been extending UPI acceptance to multiple countries as part of its Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) diplomacy, and the UPI-KHQR linkage with Cambodia is a recent example of this.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of India's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) diplomacy, with reference to UPI's expanding international linkages, in strengthening India's economic and strategic partnerships in Southeast Asia.

Examine the potential and challenges of India's trade and investment engagement with smaller ASEAN economies like Cambodia in the context of India's Act East Policy and global supply chain diversification.
